sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner invited my attention to the material on record to point out that on 19th March, 2024, the petitioner has filed P.C.R No.4389/2024 against the respondents 2 to 5 for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 166, 120B read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

In pursuance of the same, the learned Magistrate directed the matter to be referred to the jurisdictional Police Authorities for investigation under Section 156(3) of the Criminal Procedure Code vide order dated 19th April, 2024, which reads as under:
"19.04.2024 ORDER

The complainant has lodged instant complaint under Section 200 of Criminal Procedure Code for the offences punishable under Sections 406,
420, 166 and 120B read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code and has prayed this Court to refer matter to jurisdictional Police Station for carrying investigation under Section 156(3) on the accusation that the Accused has committed alleged offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 166 and 120B read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.

That, on primafacie perusal of the averments arraigned in the complaint it reveals that the offences are cognizable and non-bailable in nature, wherein the further perusal of same reveals that the Complainant at the behest had filed complaint before the Indiranagar Police Station furthermore before Commissioner of Police, by NC:
2025:KHC:5612 CRL.P NO.1632 OF 2025 setting criminal law into motion, and has maintained affidavit to that effect, wherein which on the said backdrop, it is opined that issuance of directions to Investigating Officer of Indiranagar Police Station would bring home the truth, accordingly matter referred to I.O. of Indiranagar Police Station to carry investigation as per procedure established under Section 156(3) of the Criminal Procedure Code and place report at the earliest.
Office to issue necessary directions to Investigating Officer for effective investigation and place report on or before 12.08.2024.
Await report Call on 12.08.2024."

5. It is the grievance the petitioner that, despite the aforesaid specific order directing the respondent No.1 to register the F.I.R. and conduct investigation, the respondent No.1-Police Authorities have not registered the F.I.R. even till today and as such, the petitioner is before this Court by way of present petition.

6. Learned Additional Special Public Prosecutor submits that, if the reasonable time is granted, the respondent No.1-Police Authorities will consider the order of reference dated 19th April, 2024 passed by the learned Magistrate and proceed further in accordance with law.
